title: A predictive whole-cell model for microbial design

concept.text: The proposed innovation is an integrated computational model that predicts how a microbial cell will behave from its genome and environment, including when researchers make combinations of genome changes that have never been tested. It would connect metabolism, regulation and gene expression closely enough to forecast viability, growth and molecular phenotypes, then use those predictions to guide microbial design. The goal is reliable prediction of new biological outcomes, extending beyond reproducing observations used to construct the model.

A concrete precursor is computational genome reduction: using a whole-cell model to identify combinations of genes that might be removed while preserving cellular function. Rees-Garbutt and colleagues demonstrated this approach computationally for Mycoplasma genitalium in 2020. Their study also illustrates why a successful simulation cannot by itself establish that a redesigned organism will live: the biological validity of large genome changes depends on the model's accuracy at that scale.

Proposed scope: physical organization within the cell and evolutionary constraints could also become parts of the integrated model where they materially affect prediction. These are broader ambitions retained from the research, rather than capabilities or necessary components established by the supplied study. A useful model would have an explicit domain of applicability; validation across several microbes would demonstrate generalization within tested boundaries.

significance.text: Reliable predictions of substantial genomic changes could reduce the number of organisms researchers must build and test to find a workable design. The 2020 study describes laboratory genome reduction as expensive and time-consuming, with unexpected cell death complicating the search. A sufficiently accurate model could help prioritize viable combinations and identify likely failures before construction. These are conditional benefits of improved prediction, not benefits already demonstrated across microbial engineering.

Scientific synthesis: the deeper contribution would be an integrated, experimentally falsifiable account of cellular behavior. Predicting several kinds of measurements from the same genome and environment would test whether the model's interacting mechanisms jointly explain the cell. Consistent failures could expose missing functions or mistaken assumptions, making the model an instrument for discovering biology as well as designing organisms.

Conditional downstream possibilities include more efficient development of microbial production strains, research organisms and therapeutic microbes. Reliable cellular predictions would still leave substantial work in construction, experimental characterization and application-specific development. Performance in a modeled laboratory environment would not establish robustness in an industrial process, host or ecosystem. The analogy to predictive engineering is therefore bounded by the biological contexts actually demonstrated.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target capability is dependable prediction of previously untested phenotypes after interacting genome changes and environmental shifts. Gene requirements depend on both the surrounding genome and the external environment, so results from isolated gene deletions cannot simply be added together to predict a heavily redesigned cell. The supplied study documents these obstacles, but does not establish how fully subsequent work has addressed them.

Incomplete biological knowledge creates a direct barrier to integration. The model discussed in the 2020 study did not represent 124 genes of unknown function. The authors retained those genes in their proposed in vivo designs; their absence from the simulation did not establish that living cells could dispense with them. Predicting substantial redesign therefore requires either adequate representations of consequential unknown functions or defensible limits on what the model can predict without them.

The time horizon is another consequential barrier. The study found that a cell could divide during a single simulated generation after deletions that were biologically infeasible. One division can therefore give a misleading impression of viability. Reliable design requires representing the continuing requirements of cellular function across generations, rather than treating a short simulation's success as evidence of sustained growth.

Proposed engineering requirements include connecting the component models consistently, separating biological uncertainty from simulation output, and identifying when a new genome or environment falls outside validated conditions. Physical organization and evolutionary constraints remain additional proposed modeling dimensions. The supplied evidence does not determine which representations of these dimensions are necessary, how detailed they must be, or whether their integration is the decisive remaining bottleneck.

current_state.text: In 2020, Joshua Rees-Garbutt and colleagues published Designing minimal genomes using whole-cell models. They used a Mycoplasma genitalium whole-cell model to propose reduced genomes in silico. The demonstrated achievement was computational genome design. The authors explicitly conditioned the biological success of those designs on model accuracy, which had not been tested at that scale of genetic modification; the computational results should not be presented as demonstrated living reduced genomes.

The paper's introduction reports 79% accuracy for single-gene knockout essentiality for the underlying model, attributing that result to Karr and colleagues. This is a narrow benchmark concerning whether individual gene knockouts are essential. It is not a new validation of the proposed large genome reductions, a measurement of overall whole-cell predictive accuracy, or evidence of general prediction across organisms and environments.

The study also reports 124 unmodeled genes of unknown function and identifies failures associated with the single-generation simulation horizon. Retaining the unknown-function genes in proposed biological designs acknowledges incomplete coverage. The finding that some biologically infeasible deletions still permitted simulated division further limits what can be inferred from the computational designs, without negating the demonstrated ability to search for candidate genomes in silico.

The supplied review reports access to complete, untruncated extracted text covering all 12 article pages, with no extraction issues recorded; supplementary materials were not included. Its conclusions about these results rest on textual findings and did not require figure inspection. This record relies on that supplied review and does not imply a new inspection of the paper or its supplements.

Evidence boundary: no subsequent literature or bounded freshness search was supplied to establish progress through November 1, 2026. The historical study therefore supports a computational precursor and specific limitations, but cannot establish the field's present-day frontier or prove that the broader capability remains unachieved. Absence of newer evidence here is an assessment limitation, not evidence that later advances do not exist.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: before experiments begin, a fixed model should predict viability, sustained growth and selected molecular phenotypes for genuinely new genome designs, including combinations of changes. Testing should span several species and prespecified environmental conditions, with both successes and failures reported. Such a program would establish demonstrated breadth across those cases; finite tests cannot establish literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Fixed model predicts new genome-design outcomes across several species

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evaluation: independent teams should test blinded predictions against simpler baselines using prespecified accuracy, uncertainty and failure criteria. The evaluation should distinguish prediction in familiar conditions from transfer to new genomes or environments. Numerical success thresholds would need to be selected and justified for the intended application; none are supplied here as established standards.
completion_criteria.label: Independent blinded evaluation compares predictions against simpler baselines

completion_criteria.text: Proposed persistence requirement: experimental designs should remain viable and sustain growth over multiple generations, with corresponding simulations evaluated over an appropriate time horizon. This requirement addresses the study's finding that single-generation division could survive biologically infeasible deletions. The exact number of generations and acceptable stability would need to be specified for the intended use.
completion_criteria.label: Designs remain viable and sustain growth over multiple generations

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical test: model-guided design should reach prespecified biological objectives with less empirical search than comparable baseline approaches, accounting for unsuccessful constructions and experiments. Reproducibility would require access to the model version, inputs, simulation settings, prediction records and experimental methods sufficient for independent reproduction. Reported success should identify the organisms, environments, modification types and prediction horizons for which the evidence applies.
completion_criteria.label: Model-guided design meets prespecified objectives with less empirical search

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis — MIC-01, An autonomously reproducing cell built from defined components: whole-cell prediction could guide component selection and help explain failures of constructed cells. MIC-01's defining achievement is a physically assembled reproducing cell; MIC-06's is reliable prediction and design guidance. Either achievement would require its own demonstration.

Roster-based synthesis — MIC-02, A predictive theory of microbial communities, and MIC-10, Programmable microbial consortia for durable ecosystem functions: cellular models could supply predictions about individual members. Community prediction additionally requires interactions among organisms and shared environments, while programmable consortia require experimentally durable collective functions. A predictive model of one cell does not establish either community-level capability.

Roster-based synthesis — MIC-03, Routine experimental access to microbial dark matter: access to previously difficult-to-study microbes could provide observations needed to build and test cellular models. Conversely, predictions might help suggest growth conditions. Obtaining experimental access and predicting the behavior of an accessible organism remain distinct advances.

Roster-based synthesis — MIC-04, Reliable nitrogen-fixing microbial partnerships for major cereal crops, and MIC-07, Programmable, reversible living therapies in the human microbiome: MIC-06 could help design microbial functions relevant to these applications. Reliable crop partnerships additionally depend on plant interactions and agricultural conditions; reversible living therapies require control within a host. Whole-cell design predictions alone would not establish either application.

Roster-based synthesis — MIC-05, A general platform for targeted, adaptable phage treatment, and MIC-08, Broadly effective control of bacterial antibiotic persistence: predicting bacterial responses could inform treatment or persistence research. Phage treatment also requires appropriate virus–bacterium interactions and therapeutic performance; persistence control requires explaining and altering tolerant cellular states. Neither follows automatically from growth or knockout predictions.

Roster-based synthesis — MIC-09, Forecasting horizontal gene transfer and resistance spread in microbial communities: a whole-cell model could help estimate the consequences of acquiring genes within a recipient cell. Forecasting their transfer and spread additionally requires processes operating among cells and across populations, extending beyond intracellular genome-to-phenotype prediction.

Roster-based synthesis — MIC-11, Quantifying how environmental viruses control biogeochemical fluxes: cellular models might contribute estimates of infected-cell metabolism or output. The roster concept concerns how viral effects aggregate into environmental fluxes, requiring ecological and environmental evidence beyond a whole-cell model.

Roster-based synthesis — MIC-12, A causal map from microbial metabolites to host phenotypes: MIC-06 could help predict microbial metabolite production after genome or environmental changes. Establishing how those metabolites cause host outcomes requires additional host-level causal evidence. Predicting microbial production does not establish downstream host effects.

unresolved_issues: Progress after the 2020 study, including whether later work satisfies parts of the proposed capability, cannot be assessed from the supplied evidence.
The necessity and sufficient level of detail for modeling physical organization and evolutionary constraints remain unestablished by the supplied source.
Application-specific accuracy thresholds, uncertainty criteria, multigeneration durations and acceptable stability limits remain to be defined.
The supplied evidence does not establish experimental viability of the proposed large genome reductions.
Supplementary materials were outside the supplied review; findings that would depend on them cannot be assessed here.

brief.title: Predicting how redesigned microbes will behave
possible: Researchers could predict whether a redesigned microbe would survive, grow and behave as intended before building it. A whole-cell model—a simulation linking a cell’s interacting processes—would use its genetic instructions and surroundings to forecast the effects of combinations of genetic changes never tested before.
why: Researchers could spend less time building organisms that fail. Reliable predictions would help them choose workable designs for microbes used in production, research and medicine.
The same model could help explain how cells work. When predicted behavior disagrees with experiments, the mismatch could reveal missing biological functions or mistaken assumptions.

sources.showed: They built algorithms that used an integrated cell simulation to design microbes with fewer genes. The designs worked in simulations; their survival as living organisms remained untested.
sources.quote:
We produced two genome design algorithms (Minesweeper
and the Guess/Add/Mate Algorithm (GAMA)) which use the M.
genitalium whole-cell model to generate minimal genome
designs.
sources.cited_for: The study demonstrates computational design of reduced genomes, meaning smaller sets of genetic instructions.
sources.not_established: Successful simulations did not establish that the proposed organisms could live or sustain growth.

sources.showed: They compared predicted growth with measurements in bacteria with individual genes disrupted. A simple assumption that surviving bacteria grew normally scored better. Prediction errors nevertheless led to experimentally confirmed discoveries.
sources.quote: For 84% of the strains, the specific growth rates determined by experiment and simulation were statistically indistinguishable.
sources.cited_for: The work supports experimental testing of predictions and using prediction errors to discover biology.
sources.not_established: Tests of individual gene disruptions do not establish reliable prediction of combined changes across species and environments.

sources.showed: Their whole-cell model (WCM) reproduced observed doubling behavior in a minimal bacterial cell. It linked imbalances to slower transcription, copying genes into messages, and translation, making proteins.
sources.quote: WCM reveals how emergent imbalances lead to slowdowns in the rates of transcription and translation.
sources.cited_for: The work shows that connected cell processes can reproduce aspects of a living cell’s behavior.
sources.not_established: Reproducing an existing cell’s behavior does not establish dependable forecasts for previously untested genetic redesigns.

shown: Rees-Garbutt and colleagues designed reduced genomes computationally in 2020. Some biologically infeasible deletions still allowed simulated division, showing why a short simulation can mislead.

Thornburg and colleagues later linked cellular processes in a model that reproduced observed doubling behavior. Sanghvi and colleagues also showed that disagreements between predictions and experiments could lead to biological discoveries.
missing: The target requires dependable predictions for interacting genetic changes and environmental shifts across microbes.
Models need to represent consequential unknown gene functions or establish clear limits on predictions that omit them.
Predicted survival needs experimental confirmation of sustained growth across generations.
Model-guided design needs to achieve agreed biological goals with fewer experiments than comparable approaches.

milestones.label: A fixed model predicts new designs across species
milestones.explanation: A model fixed before experiments would have to predict survival, sustained growth and molecular changes for new gene combinations across species and specified environments. This would establish its tested range.

milestones.label: Independent blinded tests establish value over simpler methods
milestones.explanation: Independent teams, unaware of prediction sources, would have to compare methods using agreed accuracy, uncertainty and failure criteria. This would test predictive value in familiar and new conditions.

milestones.label: Designed cells survive and grow across generations
milestones.explanation: Experiments would have to demonstrate sustained growth across generations, with simulations covering a corresponding period. This would distinguish lasting survival from misleading simulated division.

milestones.label: Model-guided designs reach goals with fewer experiments
milestones.explanation: Reproducible comparisons would have to show model-guided designs meeting agreed goals with less experimental search, counting failures. This would establish practical value within the tested conditions.

uncertain: The accuracy, uncertainty limits and duration of sustained growth needed for success depend on the intended use.
How much detail about a cell’s physical organization and evolutionary constraints is necessary for reliable prediction remains unclear.

page.title: Whole-cell models for microbial design
page.definition: An integrated simulation of a microbial cell predicts how genome edits and environmental changes affect growth, molecular composition and product formation. The completion benchmark is DARPA’s model-guided strain-design test for Escherichia coli K12.

goal.need: The 2020 Mycoplasma genitalium model represented 401 of 525 genes; 124 genes of unknown function were omitted. Some biologically infeasible deletions still allowed simulated division. Selecting genome edits for living strains therefore requires predictions checked against experiments, beyond finding genomes that divide in a simulation.

figures.caption: Growth-rate agreement in 86 viable M. genitalium single-gene disruption strains, reported in 2013
columns: Growth rates statistically indistinguishable from measurements
rows: Assume every strain grows at the wild-type rate
figures.note: This comparison concerns viable single-gene disruption strains and does not test combinations of deletions.

statements.body: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, Simulating Microbial Systems programme
statements.quote: The Simulating Microbial Systems (SMS) program seeks to create computational simulations that accurately predict the behavior of bacteria in various contexts.

statements.body: U.S. Department of Energy, Biological and Environmental Research programme
statements.quote: If digital twins could be quantitatively predictive, then hypotheses could be tested in silico before committing resources to physical experiments.
statements.context: The workshop report discusses computational representations of microbial cells that predict responses to genetic edits and process conditions.

completion.title: A whole-cell simulation guides a tenfold production increase in an engineered E. coli K12 strain.
completion.criterion: The same E. coli K12 simulation used for molecular and antimicrobial predictions guides strain engineering that increases production of the assigned small molecule tenfold over its initial baseline, assessed against independent wet-laboratory data.
completion.set_by: DARPA, SMS solicitation DARPA-PS-25-04, Table 4, CD2 biomanufacturing metric. The numerical threshold appears only in the table; the cited copy reproduces DARPA’s document.
completion.basis: DARPA publishes an application-level endpoint for simulation-guided engineering of a living strain. Its scope is E. coli K12 and the assigned product. It does not establish prediction across microbial species or arbitrary combinations of genome edits.

milestones.title: A reduced microbial genome supports cell division in a whole-cell simulation.
milestones.criterion: Under the Minesweeper/GAMA protocol, combined gene deletions leave a simulation that divides. In 2020, Minesweeper_256 divided in 89 of 100 simulations. In 2025, Gherman et al. reported an E. coli design retaining 737 of 1,219 modeled genes; this also remained an in silico result.
milestones.set_by: Rees-Garbutt et al., published Minesweeper/GAMA design–simulate–test protocol for M. genitalium; subsequently adapted to E. coli by Gherman et al.
milestones.threshold_quote: Simulations that produce dividing cells proceed to the next cycle, increasing the number of gene deletions and producing progressively smaller genomes.

milestones.title: A whole-cell model makes molecular predictions that biochemical assays confirm.
milestones.criterion: Model-derived predictions of enzyme catalytic rates are confirmed by purified-protein kinetic assays. Sanghvi et al. tested three M. genitalium enzymes in 2013, with three technical replicates at each of seven substrate concentrations. These results addressed molecular predictions derived from mutant growth discrepancies, rather than multi-gene strain designs.
milestones.set_by: Experimental confirmation of model predictions, applied by Stanford’s whole-cell model developers in Sanghvi et al., Figures 2–3. This is a validation convention without a universal numerical error margin.
milestones.threshold_quote: The discrepancies between simulations and experiments led to novel model predictions about specific kinetic parameters that we subsequently validated.

milestones.title: An E. coli model reproduces molecular dynamics across two networks of over 100 proteins each.
milestones.criterion: Predict all measured messenger RNA, protein and metabolite time courses, including at least two protein interaction networks with more than 100 proteins each. Independent verification and validation (IV&V) experiments establish statistical equivalence using DARPA-approved tests. In 2022, Thornburg et al. reproduced doubling behavior in JCVI-syn3A, a precursor in another organism.
milestones.set_by: DARPA SMS, Questions and Answers of 12 February 2025, answers 44 and 47; written specifically for E. coli K12.
milestones.threshold_quote: at least two (2) different protein interaction networks each comprised of >100 proteins.

milestones.title: An E. coli model predicts production rate and single-antimicrobial inhibition within ±10%.
milestones.criterion: At SMS capability demonstration CD1, predict specific production rate and the assigned single antimicrobial’s minimum inhibitory concentration within ±10% of IV&V’s experimentally determined values.
milestones.set_by: DARPA SMS solicitation, Table 4, CD1 metrics for E. coli K12. Both numerical thresholds appear only in the table.

milestones.title: An E. coli model predicts a two-antimicrobial cocktail’s inhibitory concentration within ±10%.
milestones.criterion: At SMS capability demonstration CD2, predict the minimum inhibitory concentration of a two-antimicrobial cocktail within ±10% of IV&V’s experimentally determined value.
milestones.set_by: DARPA SMS solicitation, Table 4, CD2 antimicrobial metric for E. coli K12. The numerical threshold appears only in the table.

not_found: No field-wide completion criterion covering multiple microbial species and arbitrary combinations of genome edits was found.
No public SMS result demonstrating the tenfold model-guided production endpoint was found through 14 November 2026.
Public SMS documents do not specify final equivalence margins, experimental sample sizes or whether the tenfold production measure means titer, yield or specific production rate.
The original SAM.gov solicitation attachment could not be opened; the cited GovTribe mirror reproduces DARPA’s document.
